maya: Quick heads-up — ran a cross-model perf sweep (Llama-3B / Mistral-7B / Qwen-7B) comparing FP8 / INT8 / mixed-4-bit kernels under realistic chat load with KV cache warmup. Found a pretty specific regression: when KV cache hitrate > ~80% the FP8 path drops throughput by ~18% vs the INT8 fallback on A100s.
maya: raw excerpt from the bench run:
```
model    | quant   | kv_hitrate | tokens/s | p95 latency
Llama-3B | FP8     | 0.85       | 980      | 42ms
Llama-3B | INT8    | 0.85       | 1190     | 36ms
Mistral  | FP8     | 0.60       | 1420     | 28ms
Qwen-7B  | FP8+4   | 0.82       | 860      | 48ms
```
(bench run: steady-state chat, prefix caching enabled, dynamic batching with default heuristics)

dan: Oof. Is this deterministic by model or by kernel selection path? Any kernel fallbacks or special-case kernels kicking in?

maya: Looks correlated with the FP8 GEMM kernel that expects contiguous KV loads; when KV cache is highly hitty we do a lot of small KV reads which triggers a different memory pattern and the kernel's prefetching thrashes. So kernel still used but suffers from memory stalls.

sara: Could we change the batching heuristics to prefer earlier flush for high-kv-hit sessions? Eg cap batch size to N when kv_hitrate>0.7 or switch to INT8 fallback automatically. I can sketch a patch.

oliver: Also wonder if quant profiles should embed a per-model "kv_sensitivity" flag so the router/runtime can pick tune sets automatically. Something like `/profiles/quant/llama-3b.kv-aware.json`.

maya: Agreed. I added a draft PR with two things: (1) a batcher heuristic tweak (cap +kv-aware priority) (2) a routing hook that annotates requests with `quant_reliability` so we can toggle fallbacks in routing policy. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/profiles/pull/451

ci-bot: perf-check failed on one benchmark: `Llama-3B FP8 steady-state throughput` -- regression +16% vs baseline. See: https://ci.redwood.ai/runs/98765

lee: For safety let's do a canary rollout: config toggle in Dedicated that flips batcher to the new heuristic for 5% of traffic on infra-dev region. Add an A/B comparison for latency and token-cost.

maya: Will do. Next steps for me: 1) push an explicit per-model quant profile for Llama/Mistral/Qwen with `kv_sensitivity` and `recommended_fallback` fields; 2) add canary config and perf dashboards; 3) run longer 24h load test. I'll drop the profile names in this thread when pushed.

dan: Thx. If you want I can help with kernel microbench to try a different prefetch strategy (simulate smaller reads) and test impact.

maya: Yes please — assign to you in the PR. Also attaching a quick snippet we used to reproduce (local run):
```
PYTHONPATH=. ./bench/run_chat_bench.py --model llama-3b --quant fp8 --kv-prefill 512 --clients 64 --duration 600
```

sara: Cool — I'll also add a note to /eng-ml/ops-runbook about watching CI perf-checks for these quant-related PRs :eyes:

oliver: When profiles land, I'll update the Optimize recommender so it surfaces `kv_sensitivity` warnings to customers (suggest INT8 fallback for high-kv workloads).

maya: Final: pushed `profiles/quant/llama-3b.kv-aware.v1.json`, `profiles/quant/mistral-7b.kv-aware.v1.json`, and `profiles/quant/qwen-7b.kv-aware.v1.json` to the PR branch. Link above. Leaving the thread open for kernel bench results and canary metrics.
